questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A good mix of a good university as well as a fun city to explore

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We studied too much, because we were not used to not having block structure. Going from 2 to 6 courses as well as having Master's courses is hard to adapt to

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It is fine, just write to your erasmus coordinator they will help. There is a lot of back and forth, and not being sure about things, but it will work out eventually.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Primarily through Erasmus coordinator

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: We live at one of the dorms. Can recommend 17. listopadu dorm

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Bad cooking facilities, you share a tiny kitchen with 3 other people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Its pretty frugal. Rent is cheap, but it's safe to say it's not a cozy and great home you get to live in. If you have money, seek something else, if you dont care, and want to save money, dorm is way to go. Also great way to meet new people

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: its easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You need to enroll in courses. Enroll in good time, some courses may get filled up before you have a chance.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not so much, but its pretty intuitive.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It worked, we were on waiting list for some of the courses in the first week, but we still attended, and people unenrolled, and then we got a spot.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: enroll fast

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very exciting courses, but the course structure is way more analog and less digital. Things may not be up to date on teaching platforms, and we often got surprises for the exams, website and course site says one thing, but exam is something else.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is somewhat the same as in UCPH. What can surprise you is the amount of focus you need to allocate to different things, having 2 focuses over 8 weeks is not the same as having 6 focus over 16 weeks. This needs more discipline, structure, and also more work, there are more assignments per week, etc.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Same. There are lectures, there are labs. Its way smaller classes in most courses. You can get to know the professor much easilier, and there is not the notion of TA's for exercise lessons, it's still just the professor.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All courses were very interesting. I would recommend highly for you, to take the language course 3 weeks before your semester starts. You can get 5 credits/ECTS for it, you meet people, you can talk the local language better, and less stress from school. I did not do it, and I would change that if I did exchange again. 

Generally, take what sounds interesting for you, but if you can, take courses that give more credits. The semester was honestly very very hard because of the more courses, and the courses did not feel smaller even though they credit less points.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: its pretty similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open, people are in a similar situation as you, and people are nice.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not anything big.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I cant say to be honest. In academia, I like that the professors have more respect, you should call them Professor *lastname*, which can be hard to pronounce, but you will get the hang of it. Very sweet people, but they have earned their title. It is more traditional on several points.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Think about what you want out of the semester. We know people that took 3 courses 10 ects each, and of course, had a lot more time to do social and cultural activities than me, having 6 x 5 ECTS courses.  There are some very exciting courses, but think about this. Not having block structure and going from 2 to 6 courses can definitely surprise you and take time from you. If you are leaning towards more social activities, take the language course. it's 3 weeks of learning the language, meeting other exchange students, and shaving 5 ECTS of the 30 you need to take.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I had not moved out before, so learning to be more independant was a very cool experience. You will meet a lot of funny crazy people from very different walks of live, invite it in and let new experiences shape you that you otherwise have less opportunity to do.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: School workload.
